take: Hurricane Isaias has shut in 1.46 million b/d of US Gulf oil production, 71% of the region's output, which is the dominant crude headline even as Washington and Tehran talk peace and China signals it will resume refined fuel exports. The second theme is the shipping crisis proper: supertanker rates have soared to record highs as the Iran war reshuffles trade routes and ties up tonnage in inefficient voyages, whilst the IEA's fresh 100 million barrel release of diesel, gasoline and crude risks draining the world's last supply cushion. Positioning-wise, the US lifting of sanctions on Russian diesel for six months via General License 135, with EU and UK measures unchanged, plus extra Russian and German barrels, should soften the distillate squeeze that record US crude output of 13.8 million b/d cannot fix. The cross-market link to watch is product tanker earnings versus bunker economics, with FSL offloading another veteran product tanker and Larine clearing its two LR1s to UAE interests for $110m, signalling asset values are running hot into the dislocation. In the next 24 hours watch Isaias landfall damage assessments and any MMS restart guidance, the Panama Canal's post-earthquake inspections given transits are still running, and whether the Iran peace chatter gains enough traction to cap the hurricane bid.
